title: Multi modal perceived conversation success prediction for spontaneous autistic and non-autistic dyadic interactions
abstract: arXiv:2610.31682v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Conversation success is important for communication, social bonds, and well-being and is often reduced in autistic-neurotypical conversations. Previous studies have predicted perceived conversation success using acoustic and lexical features in pediatric autism-enriched samples, or using nonverbal behavior in non-autistic group interactions. Other work has characterized prosodic, facial, motor, and turn-taking synchrony in autistic interactions, but has primarily targeted diagnostic classification or group differences. The present study instead predicts participant perceived conversation success from complementary articulatory, facial, acoustic-prosodic, and turn-taking measures across three spontaneous dyadic-interaction datasets including autistic and non autistic individuals. By leveraging multimodal features, we demonstrate that conversational success is inherently multidimensional and requires a multi-faceted analytical framework. C

translated_title: 针对自闭症与非自闭症个体自发双人对话互动的多模态感知对话成功预测
translated_abstract: 对话成功对于沟通、社会纽带和幸福感至关重要，而在自闭症者与神经典型者的对话中，对话成功往往会降低。先前的研究曾在儿科自闭症富集样本中使用声学和词汇特征来预测感知的对话成功，或在非自闭症群体互动中使用非言语行为进行预测。其他研究刻画了自闭症互动中的韵律、面部、动作和话轮转换同步性，但主要针对诊断分类或组间差异分析。本研究则从互补的构音、面部、声学-韵律和话轮转换测量出发，在三个包含自闭症和非自闭症个体的自发双人互动数据集上预测参与者感知的对话成功。通过利用多模态特征，我们证明对话成功本质上是多维的，需要一个多层面的分析框架。
tldr: 本研究提出利用构音、面部、声学-韵律和话轮转换等多模态特征，在包含自闭症与非自闭症个体的自发双人对话数据中预测参与者感知的对话成功，证明对话成功本质上是多维的，需要多层面的分析框架。
en_tdlr: This study leverages complementary articulatory, facial, acoustic-prosodic, and turn-taking features to predict perceived conversation success in spontaneous dyadic interactions between autistic and non-autistic individuals, demonstrating that conversational success is inherently multidimensional and requires a multi-faceted analytical framework.
